title: Making Postgres 300x faster for analytics: batching, operator fusion, and SIMD
summary: This article describes how the author optimized PostgreSQL's query engine to achieve 300x performance improvements for analytical queries using three key techniques: batching (processing multiple rows together instead of one at a time), operator fusion (combining multiple operators into single passes), and SIMD instructions (utilizing CPU vector processing capabilities for parallel data operations).
problem_solved: PostgreSQL's traditional tuple-at-a-time execution model creates excessive overhead for analytical workloads, making it inefficient compared to specialized OLAP databases.
why_valuable: It demonstrates how fundamental architectural changes in query execution can unlock massive performance gains without changing the SQL interface or compatibility.
